subject: Post-call: Model fit & evals follow-up — FinLytics / Next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Model fit & evals follow-up — FinLytics / Next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off a focused eval: 

Recap:
- Goal: Evaluate model fit for FinLytics’ financial summarization & Q&A flows (300-1k token summaries; high factuality).
- Success metrics: ROUGE-style recall for extractive summaries, structured-field accuracy (JSON schema compliance) for models that output trades/instruments, and latency < 220ms p50 on x86-4 GPU for 512 tokens.

 Recommended initial models / configs:
- redwood-turbo-3b (baseline, higher throughput)
- redwood-xt-13b-4bit (quality-focused, quantized option)
- vendor-model-a (for comparison; we'll treat as external baseline)

Artifacts attached: mutual action plan + prompt set v1 (see attachments). Prompt set contains representative prompts and expected JSON schema for structured outputs.

Technical eval focus (tool/function calling & structured output):
- JSON schema compliance: we’ll run structured-output evals that validate model outputs against your schema and measure failure modes (missing keys, wrong types, extra fields).
- Retries & deterministic post-processing: define retry policy for transient decoding failures; capture when retries change semantic content.
- Tools: function-calling harness will simulate API calls for entity-resolution and price-lookups. We'll log call traces for root-cause.

Proposed next steps:
1) You: share a small representative dataset (100-200 examples) with expected JSON outputs and a sample of prompts by EOD Tue. Drive link is fine.
2) Us: stand up a 2-week eval run (benchmarks + prompt sweep) and share results + recommendations.
3) Sync: 30-min technical kickoff (we recommend Wed 10–11am PT).

Attachments: [Attachment: FinLytics_MA_plan.pdf], [Attachment: finlytics_prompt_set_v1.json]

Thanks — I’ll book the kickoff once you confirm availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we share data: 

1) JSON schema: our legal team insists we maintain strict schemas for reporting outputs. Can you confirm whether your structured-output eval will surface the exact schema mismatches (e.g., type vs missing key) and a sample of failing outputs? We’ll need that for our audit trail.

2) Retries: what retry behavior are you proposing? For our production flows we only allow 1 retry and we need to understand if retries will materially change extracted values (especially numeric fields).

3) Data sharing: we can upload a redacted set (~150 examples) to the Drive folder (I’ll share the link). Is that sufficient for the initial run? Also — are there any specific formatting rules for the expected outputs you need?

Also, security question: do you have a SOC 2 attestation we can share with procurement?

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Data & ML | FinLytics
elena.torres@finlytics.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & evals follow-up — FinLytics / Next steps

Hi Elena — quick answers from the engineering side: 

1) Schema mismatch reporting: yes — our structured-output evaluator will produce per-example diffs indicating: missing keys, extra keys, type mismatches, and value-level assertion failures. Example output in the report will include the raw model output, normalized JSON (best-effort parse), and an error code for the mismatch. We’ll also provide a failure-rate histogram by key so you can prioritize schema fixes.

2) Retries: we recommend starting with 1 retry (so at most 2 attempts total). We’ll capture both attempts in the eval and report on cases where the retry changed a numeric value by >1% or changed enum fields. For critical numeric fields we can also enable deterministic decoding (top-p annealing) to reduce variance during the eval.

3) Sample formatting: please include the expected JSON in a column called "expected_output" (stringified JSON is fine) and a separate "prompt_template" column. CSV or NDJSON both work; we prefer NDJSON for large-scale runs. The attached prompt_set_v1 JSON shows our recommended schema examples.

Security / SOC 2: Marissa — can you attach the SOC 2 cert?

Tech resources for you: 
- Eval dashboard (internal): https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/finlytics-eval-202705
- Structured-output evaluator docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/structured-output-evals

Happy to discuss specifics on the kickoff.

—Rishi
Director, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
